case_name: Fact piece about a real thing
title: Meet the Real F-35A
tests: Tests whether a short factual aircraft film preserves the named variant's visible geometry and operating characteristics.

faults.what: The supplied speech transcript contains only the Italian phrase “Un saluto.” The required English explanation of one engine and conventional runway takeoff is absent.
The aircraft remains suspended sideways above the runway in every sampled frame, with its landing gear extended. No forward runway roll or conventional lift-off is shown.
The aircraft has distorted wing and rear-fuselage geometry rather than convincing real F-35A proportions, and no clearly recognizable single rear engine exhaust is visible.
Wing and rear-body shapes change between frames, undermining aircraft-design consistency.
Unrequested blocks of garbled white text appear at the left and lower left near the end, and the aircraft carries malformed lettering.

judge.summary: The widescreen clip presents the three correct labels, but shows a distorted aircraft suspended over a runway and lacks the requested takeoff sequence and English narration.

must_haves.item: The aircraft has the recognizable F-35 configuration: one rear engine exhaust, two outward-canted vertical tails and no canards.
must_haves.why: Paired tails are visible, but the distorted rear geometry does not show a recognizable single engine exhaust, and the overall aircraft is not a convincing real F-35A.

must_haves.item: The takeoff shows a forward runway roll and lift-off, not hovering or a vertical launch.
must_haves.why: All four samples show the aircraft already suspended above the runway, pointed across rather than along it; none shows a runway roll or conventional lift-off.

must_haves.item: The same aircraft design remains consistent between the runway and airborne views.
must_haves.why: There is no grounded runway view establishing the transition, and the wing and rear-fuselage geometry visibly changes across the airborne samples.

must_haves.item: All three requested labels appear exactly and are legible.
must_haves.why: The three main overlay labels are legible and match the requested wording, appearing in the requested order.

must_haves.item: Audible English narration correctly describes one engine and conventional runway takeoff without attributing F-35B hover capability to the F-35A.
must_haves.why: The supplied transcript reports only “Un saluto,” not English narration explaining either requested fact.

title: Seed Growth With Supplied Narration
tests: Tests whether a supplied script becomes verbatim audible narration synchronized with an explanatory visual sequence.

exact_text.text: A seed takes in water. Roots grow downward, and a shoot reaches up toward the light.
exact_text.read_as: A seed takes in water. Roots grow downward and a shoot reaches up toward the light.

faults.what: The required instructional sequence is not established: the first sampled frame already has roots and a tall leafy shoot, and none of the supplied frames shows water reaching the seed.

The animation visibly morphs rather than consistently depicting germination: a soil column appears beneath the seed, the background changes from a room to an ocean-like scene, and narrow leaves become broad leaves.
The oversized red, double-lobed seed looks more like paired fruit or bulbs, making the intended seed anatomy unclear.

judge.summary: The eight-second clip has the correct narration but shows an already-sprouted, morphing plant rather than a clear, ordered explanation of germination.

must_haves.item: One approximately 8-second widescreen video shows an animated seed sprouting.
must_haves.why: The supplied clip is eight seconds and widescreen, with a seed-like object whose roots and shoot develop across the frames.

must_haves.item: The audible voice-over says the supplied script verbatim, without extra spoken lines.
must_haves.why: The supplied speech transcription matches the requested words and contains no extra spoken lines; the omitted comma does not alter the spoken script.

must_haves.item: Water reaches the seed, roots grow downward, and a shoot grows upward toward light in that order.
must_haves.why: No water delivery is visible, and both roots and a substantial shoot are already present at one second. The required progression toward light is not demonstrated.

must_haves.item: The corresponding growth stages appear while the narration describes them.
must_haves.why: The opening sampled image already shows a leafy shoot and exposed roots rather than the initial water-uptake stage described at the start of the narration.

must_haves.item: There is no on-screen text or music.
must_haves.why: No on-screen text appears in the supplied frames, but the audio information does not establish whether music is absent.

case_name: A film brief the agent already made on the free tier: the economists' video podcast
title: Two economists, a 30 s video podcast
tests: Tests whether a system can turn a story brief with two named characters and four spoken lines into a 30-second film: characters that persist across shots, audible dialogue that carries the argument, and a staged studio.

faults.what: The supplied audio transcription contains only one line about government spending in a recession, rather than two spoken lines per host. Leo's opposing argument and the spoken closing disagreement are missing.
Dark labels across the front of the table contain visibly garbled lettering that changes between frames.
An additional mug appears in the woman's raised hand at 11.3 seconds while she still holds another mug on the table, creating a distracting prop-continuity anomaly.

judge.summary: The film achieves a warm, live-action podcast setting with consistent hosts, but delivers only one audible line instead of the requested four-line economic debate.

must_haves.item: Two hosts, a woman and a man, are on screen at microphones in a cosy studio with a live-action look, not animation.
must_haves.why: Both hosts appear at microphones in a warmly lit studio with curtains, bookshelves, and a realistic live-action appearance.

must_haves.item: Each host is heard speaking two short lines: Maya argues the government should spend in a recession to restore demand; Leo argues spending and cheap money cause boom and bust and the economy should correct itself.
must_haves.why: The only transcribed speech is the government-spending argument. Neither four spoken lines nor Leo's argument is present in the supplied audio evidence.

must_haves.item: The lines are audible speech, not only music or silence.
must_haves.why: One audible spoken sentence is explicitly reported, although the remaining required dialogue is missing.

must_haves.item: The two hosts stay the same people across the shots.
must_haves.why: The woman and man retain consistent facial appearance, hair, and clothing across the four frames.

must_haves.item: It ends on a friendly disagreement between them.
must_haves.why: The closing frame shows friendly smiles and a subtitle expressing disagreement, but the supplied speech transcription does not contain a closing exchange or audible disagreement.

must_haves.item: About 30 seconds, widescreen 16:9.
must_haves.why: The clip is reported as 30 seconds long, and the supplied frames are 16:9.

case_name: A 10-second product ad with a closing line (the live bench's film brief)
title: Cabin Coffee, 10 s YouTube ad
tests: Tests a short ad from a one-line brief: a staged product moment, a human action, and an exact closing line on screen.

faults.what: The main sequence shows a second mug tilted over the table mug, initially pouring into it, rather than clearly showing the table mug being picked up.
The end card switches to a different, light-coloured plaid mug and a grey-sleeved hand, breaking continuity with the dark mug and bare arm.
The supplied audio transcript reports an unrelated spoken utterance, "شايبوسي.", which does not support the requested coffee message.

judge.summary: A warm coffee spot with the correct branded closing line, but an unrequested two-mug pouring sequence replaces the intended simple pickup.

must_haves.item: A steaming mug on a wooden table in dawn light is the opening image.
must_haves.why: The opening sample shows a mug on a wooden table, visible steam, and warm early-morning-style window light, although a second mug is already being tipped above it.

must_haves.item: A hand lifts the mug.
must_haves.why: A hand holds a mug raised above the table, including in the closing image, though a continuous pickup of the opening table mug is not shown.

must_haves.item: The words 'Wake up slow' appear on screen at the end, spelled exactly.
must_haves.why: The closing card clearly reads "Wake up slow".

must_haves.item: The mood is warm and quiet (no fast cuts, no loud colours).
must_haves.why: The supplied frames use warm light, muted colours, and a restrained composition, with the same kitchen setup maintained across the first three samples.

must_haves.item: About 10 seconds, widescreen 16:9.
must_haves.why: The clip is reported as 10.7 seconds and the supplied frames are widescreen 16:9.

case_name: A one-minute explainer with a fixed sequence of facts: the citric acid cycle
title: Citric acid cycle, a 60 s explainer
tests: Tests a one-minute explainer with a fixed order of facts: whether the system keeps one consistent diagram across a minute, letters short labels correctly, narrates the steps in order, and stays within the length.

exact_text.read_as: Not visible in the supplied frames.

faults.what: The narration contains misleading biology: it associates FADH2 production with fumarate becoming FADH2 and says oxaloacetate yields another carbon dioxide group. These confuse the reactions and the regeneration step.

Several diagram annotations are garbled or incomplete, including 'ANADH', an unreadable enzyme annotation near fumarate, and leader lines without labels. Key intermediates and products are not consistently identifiable.
The illustration uses heavily shaded, textured, three-dimensional-looking organelles and molecular blobs rather than the requested simple, clean 2D animation.
Some annotations are clipped or crowded against the frame edges, including the final CO2 label at the top.
The runtime is approximately 66 seconds rather than 60 seconds.

judge.summary: The video presents a mitochondrial cycle diagram with English narration, but inaccurate explanations and garbled labels make it unsuitable for first-year teaching without a redo.

must_haves.item: The cycle is shown as a loop, as a simple clean 2D animation inside a mitochondrion, not live action.
must_haves.why: A loop appears inside an illustrated mitochondrion, but the textured, dimensional rendering and cluttered annotations do not satisfy the simple clean 2D requirement.

must_haves.item: The steps appear in order: acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to form citrate; two carbons leave as CO2; NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced; oxaloacetate is regenerated.
must_haves.why: The narration broadly follows the cycle and the final caption gives the expected totals, but malformed reaction descriptions and the erroneous final oxaloacetate statement prevent a clear, correct presentation of the required sequence.

must_haves.item: Calm English narration is audible and explains each step as it happens.
must_haves.why: English speech is documented, but its fragmented and scientifically misleading descriptions do not adequately explain each step. Calmness and precise synchronization cannot be established from the transcript.

must_haves.item: The key molecules are labelled on screen as they appear, and the title 'Citric acid cycle' is shown.
must_haves.why: Some labels are readable, including citrate, fumarate, oxaloacetate and ATP, but others are garbled or absent, and the required title is not visible in the supplied frames.

must_haves.item: About 60 seconds, widescreen 16:9.
must_haves.why: The supplied frames are 16:9 and the approximately 66-second runtime is reasonably close to one minute.

must_haves.item: No music.
must_haves.why: The speech transcription does not establish whether background music is present; the filename alone is not evidence.
